security_audit.summary: Most static shell-execution findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, not executable Ruby or shell backticks. The remaining concerns are real configuration risks: unpinned npx package execution examples and token-style credential placeholders in MCP environment blocks.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx package execution in MCP examples
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, verify package publishers, and require user confirmation before running generated MCP install commands.

remediation.issue: Credential placeholders appear inside generated environment configuration examples
remediation.suggestion: Show references to environment variables or secret managers instead of token-shaped values or raw API key placeholders.

remediation.issue: MCP command examples lack explicit safety checks
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to review command source, package permissions, and required token scopes before enabling an MCP server.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned MCP Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill examples use npx with package-name@latest and github-mcp@latest for MCP server commands. This can execute newly published package code without version pinning or publisher verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command and args fields directly configure npx package execution with latest tags. This is a clear supply-chain risk if copied into an active MCP setup.

content.value_statement: MCP setup can be hard to structure and secure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through MCP configurations, authentication patterns, testing, and performance review.
actual_capabilities: Drafts MCP server configuration patterns for APIs, databases, cloud services, and developer tools.
Explains authentication requirements and required environment variables for MCP services.
Suggests performance improvements such as connection pooling, retries, and error handling.
Provides MCP integration examples for GitHub-style API connectors.
Lists testing and validation checks for MCP server configurations.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not include executable implementation code.
Examples use placeholder package names and tokens that require security review before use.
It does not verify package provenance, package versions, or server compatibility.
It does not test generated MCP configurations automatically.

use_cases.title: Create a Service MCP
use_cases.description: Plan a new MCP server configuration for an API, database, or cloud service integration.

use_cases.title: Standardize MCP Configuration
use_cases.description: Define consistent server naming, command structure, environment variables, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Review MCP Security
use_cases.description: Check authentication, token handling, command safety, and permission boundaries before rollout.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic MCP Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a known service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic MCP server plan for [service]. Include the server name, required environment variables, setup steps, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Add Authentication Guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup that needs secure credentials.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design MCP authentication for [service]. Identify required token scopes, safe secret storage, rotation steps, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize MCP Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this MCP integration for performance. Suggest improvements for connection reuse, retries, rate limits, logging, and response validation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit MCP Rollout Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this MCP rollout plan. Flag command execution risk, package trust issues, credential handling gaps, and missing test coverage.

output_examples.output: A concise plan with server purpose, package selection notes, required token scopes, endpoint details, install cautions, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Optimize this MCP server for performance.
output_examples.output: A review covering connection reuse, retry limits, response validation, logging, rate limits, and load testing.

output_examples.input: Review MCP authentication for a database connector.
output_examples.output: A risk review that identifies secret storage issues, least-privilege access, rotation steps, and confirmation points.

best_practices: Pin MCP package versions and verify publisher trust before adding commands to configurations.
Use environment variables or secret managers instead of storing token values in shared files.
Test each MCP server in a limited environment before granting broad repository or cloud access.
anti_patterns: Installing MCP packages with latest tags in unattended workflows.
Embedding personal access tokens directly in generated configuration files.
Granting broad API scopes before the integration has a clear access model.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create MCP integration plans, configuration patterns, authentication guidance, and performance review checklists.

faq.question: Does this skill run MCP servers?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but it does not execute commands or test servers by itself.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I review before using generated commands?
faq.answer: Review package source, version pinning, publisher trust, token scopes, and local execution permissions.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or a secret manager. Avoid placing raw token values in shared configuration files.

faq.question: Is this skill best for new or existing MCP projects?
faq.answer: It can support both. Use it to plan new integrations or review existing configurations for security and performance.
